newsitem.title: CHINA: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - April 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - April 10.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Chinese political and business stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Beijing. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (8610) 6532-1921. Fax: (8610) 6532-4978.
- Premier Li Peng says world business community will have to weather tough competition to get the chance to enter the Chinese market.
- Vice-Premier Zhu Rongji says he hopes the World Bank will continue to support China in economic construction.
- China's securities regulators will block the issuance of unauthorised covertible bonds and could fine companies that violate its rules.
- The central bank sets new rules to monitor large cash withdrawals from the nation's banks.
- The central bank orders a temporary halt to use of time deposits as collateral for borrowing.
- People's Insurance Company of China Property offers a $1.2 billion policy to cover the Lingao Nuclear Plant.
- The central bank's Shenzhen branch bans futures brokerages from engaging in securities business. It also bans bank stock brokerages from conducting out-of-town business.
- The Shenzhen Development Bank launches a down payment scheme for people to buy cars.
- China bans imports of pork from Germany and pork and beef from the Netherlands.

- Vice-Minister of Construction Tan Qinglian calls for more efforts to fight corruption in the building industry that has been largely responsible for inferior building quality and serious structural collapses.
